text:
Rep. Young Kim questions U.S. officials on Haiti gang crisis strategy in hearing
C. J. Dodge
Congresswoman Young Kim participated in a House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing titled “Confronting Haiti’s Terrorist Gangs: The Gang Suppression Force and the Path Ahead” on July 21 in Washington, D.C.
During the hearing, Ambassador Michael Kozak of the U.S. Department of State and Colonel Justin Gorkowski of the Department of Defense testified about ongoing United States efforts to help restore security and stability in Haiti. Violent gangs have seized control of much of Haiti's capital, displacing more than one million people.
Kim questioned administration officials regarding recruitment and training efforts for thousands of new Haitian National Police officers. She also pressed for an update on when Haiti’s security forces would be prepared to assume primary responsibility for restoring order.
Young Kim is currently serving in the U.S. Congress, representing California’s 40th district after replacing previous member Gil Cisneros in 2021, according to the official congressional website. She previously served in the California State Assembly from 2014 to 2016 and graduated from the University of Southern California with a BBA.
Kim was born in Incheon, South Korea, in 1962 and currently lives in La Habra.
